details: CONFIRMED by reading holds_test: name = rest.split("::")[-1]; the middle part is dropped. Correct per the brief, which asks only that the
function be defined in the file, so this is LOW: a mistyped class name passes both gates, and the checker that later runs the recorded
test gets a collection error instead of a test. Size: 10 agent minutes (for a .py file with three parts, also require
r"\bclass\s+<Class>\b" in source; add the case to CASES).
evidence: lib/relay_queue.py:841-845: path, _, rest = test.strip().partition("::"); name = rest.split("::")[-1].strip(); ... return _holds_test(path.strip(), name, source)
failing_case: returns True today (only the last :: part is matched), and both relay queue done and the merge guard accept it, while
pytest tests/t.py::NoSuchClass::test_hangs_within_bound reports "not found". A stricter rule would return False.
fix_hint: In holds_test, when path ends with .py and rest has two parts, also require re.search(r"\bclass\s+" + re.escape(cls) + r"\b", source).
pass_cases: holds_test("tests/t.sh::case_x", "case_x() { :; }") -> True (non-.py files keep the whole-word rule, no class check)
findings.summary: holds_test ignores the Class part, so a recorded file::WrongClass::name that pytest cannot run is accepted by both callers

notes: Fine: holds_test takes the whole <file>::[Class::]name, strips, refuses an empty file part, an empty name and a missing file (source None),
and delegates to the old _holds_test, so done() keeps its old verdicts and the guard now uses the same rule (whole-word def for .py,
whole word otherwise). The guard previously accepted a substring (tests/t.py::test_hangs against def test_hangs_within_bound) and refused
Class::name; both are now fixed and the merge test case table encodes both, so TestMergeJudges fails with the old substring rule
(traced: "Suite::test_hangs_within_bound" is not literal text of SOURCE; "test_hangs" is). TestDoneJudges cannot fail with the fix disabled,
because done() was already right; it is the pass-case side of the brief ("from BOTH callers"), which is acceptable.
meta["test"] is a non-empty string whenever the guard reaches the check (parse flags closed_at without a test), so holds_test never gets None.
The guard only re-judges items the range adds to done/, so items closed earlier under the substring rule are not re-checked.
Small divergence left: done() reads the file at the unstripped path while holds_test and the guard strip it; done is the stricter side, so no
name done records is refused by the guard.
